deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 91 is a continuous German prose passage in Kurrent script. It reads like lecture or reading notes on ancient Greek history, possibly not in Gauss's own hand. It continues the previous page's account of Alcibiades and the Peloponnesian War and narrates the Athenian Sicilian Expedition (415–413 BC):

(1) Against the advice of sensible statesmen, Alcibiades' project was approved. A fleet with 10,000 picked troops was fitted out under Nicias, Lamachus and Alcibiades. A marginal 'Nicias' in different ink corrects a struck-out spelling in the text.
(2) The fleet sailed from Athens in 415 and reached Rhegium without mishap.
(3) While the generals deliberated, Alcibiades was recalled because his enemies had brought charges against him. He embarked, took his chance to escape, and went over to Sparta.
(4) The other two generals hesitated, which gave Syracuse time to raise cavalry and fortify the city.
(5) In 414 the Athenians began a siege lasting about a year and a half and built a wall around the city. Their attacks were repulsed, and Athens sent a second fleet of 70 ships.
(6) The Syracusans received help from Sparta under Gylippus. Superscript numerals 2 and 3 and the marginal word 'Hülfe' reorder this sentence. The date is given as 413. Gylippus got into the city and revived the inhabitants' courage.
(7) The Athenians ('Athener' is written above a struck-out 'Spartaner') had taken part of the city but were driven back.
(8) They wanted to withdraw, but the Syracusans blockaded them in the harbour. A stubborn battle was fought at the harbour mouth, and by evening the Athenians fell back to their positions. The narrative continues on folio 92 with the retreat and surrender.

No computation is made, no mathematical problem is addressed, and no implicit steps need filling in.
errors: Historical, not mathematical: Gylippus reached Syracuse in late summer/autumn 414 BC, not 413. The arrival of the second Athenian relief fleet under Demosthenes belongs to 413.
'Eine Flotte mit 10000 Mann' is a rough figure. Thucydides (6.43) gives 134 triremes and about 5,100 hoplites plus light troops, roughly 6,400 fighting men excluding rowers.
The relief fleet is given as 70 ships. Thucydides gives 73 (7.42), so this is a minor rounding.
The page does not record that Lamachus fell in 414 during the siege. 'Die übrigen beiden' is therefore accurate only for the early phase.

The battle 'am Eingange des Hafens' is a simplification. The decisive Athenian defeat was in the Great Harbour, as they tried to break the Syracusan boom at its mouth, so the statement is roughly correct.

results.what: Narrative summary of the Athenian Sicilian Expedition 415–413 BC (non-mathematical history notes)
results.modern_name: Sicilian Expedition (Peloponnesian War), after Thucydides books 6–7
results.usually_credited_to: Thucydides (primary source); standard school/university history curriculum c. 1800

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds only school-level ancient history notes on the Sicilian Expedition, with no mathematical content. The handwriting and subject suggest notes possibly by a family member or student bound into the bundle, but in any case nothing here bears on Gauss's mathematics.

checkable.asserts: The expedition spanned the archon-year interval 415 BC to 413 BC, consistent with a siege begun in 414 lasting about one and a half years.

transcription_corrections: 'Er stellte sich ein[?], sahe aber die Gefahr[?] wohl[?] und entfloh' more likely reads 'Er schiffte sich ein, nahm aber die Gelegenheit wahr und entfloh'. This is historically apt: Alcibiades embarked for Athens and escaped at Thurii.
The right-margin word 'Nicias' is in different (brownish) ink and replaces the struck-out spelling in line 4. The in-text reading should be marked as a marginal correction.

In the Gylippus sentence, the superscript numerals 2 and 3 over 'von Sparta' and 'bekommen', together with the marginal 'Hülfe', signal a reordering. The intended reading is roughly 'allein die Syracusaner bekamen 413 Hülfe von Sparta unter Gylippus'.
'Athener' is written as a superscript above the struck-out 'Spartaner'. The transcription has this right, but it should note the superscript placement.
'Reuterei' (archaic spelling of Reiterei) appears correct; the [?] can be dropped.
In 'eines Theils der Stadt bemächtigt' the struck-out word before 'einmal' appears as 'schon [einmal]'. The image supports 'schon' followed by a struck-out 'einmal'.
